description: The hand-verified expected outcome for oss-scan-results/adapter-tests/fixtures/halt-trivy-declared-findings-unheld.json. It states a HALT, not rows. Every value was derived by reading the fixture and the authored contracts in harness/lib/normalize/adapters/trivy.py, never by running the adapter and recording its traceback.
outcome_kind: adapter structural-validation halt, after successful routing and before a single row is built
scanner_class: per record -- vuln, secret or misconfig -- taken from the section array a record was read from. No record is ever assigned one here, because the halt precedes row construction.

derived_from.that_fixture_is: the byte-for-byte capture of harness/artifacts/raw/trivy.json, sha256 4551d6ca435ad71aa2306bd03aa45ce92ba95d5f9ee03f304767f9f791878eba, 3,496 bytes, three Results[] elements each holding exactly one DS-0026 Misconfigurations record
derived_from.what_changed: Results[1]'s Misconfigurations array was emptied -- the single DS-0026 record was removed and the member left in place as [] -- while its MisconfSummary still declares Successes 26 and Failures 1. That is the shape a truncated or post-filtered artifact has: the element's own summary says a check failed and no section holds the failure.
derived_from.derivation_check: diff fixtures/trivy.json against this file: the only difference is that Results[1].Misconfigurations is [] where the capture has one record. Both MisconfSummary members are untouched, which is what makes the contradiction internal to the artifact rather than something this file asserts about it.
derived_from.nothing_else_changed: the report envelope, all three Targets, all three MisconfSummary objects and the DS-0026 records on Results[0] and Results[2] are the capture's, byte for byte. The empty array is deliberately the present-and-empty shape rather than a removed key: an implementation checking only whether the member exists would miss it.
derived_from.formatting: written with the capture's own one-space JSON indentation and, like the capture, with no trailing newline, so a byte diff against fixtures/trivy.json shows the structural change and nothing else.

fixture.fixture_is_never_edited_to_suit_this_fil: This expectation is re-derived when the fixture changes, which the recorded sha256 above makes visible. The fixture is the input and this file is the assertion; the dependency runs one way.

field_order_authority: harness/lib/normalize/emit.py, the FIELDS constant. Recorded for parity with the positive expected files in this folder; no row below carries it.
row_level_policy_keys_absent: absence_permitted_fields, absence_convention and severity_norm_vocabulary are deliberately not carried here: each is a policy about the content of an emitted row and this file expects no row.

routing.is_sarif_derivation: shape.is_sarif requires a mapping whose version is the exact string "2.1.0" together with a runs array. This document is a mapping carrying neither member, so the conjunction is False on both halves and the shape is native.
routing.scanner_class_from_routing: the PER_RECORD sentinel shape.SCANNER_CLASS_BY_TOOL holds for trivy, for which shape.is_per_record returns True
routing.not_a_shape_failure: The failure here is NOT shape.UnknownArtifactShape. The document's top level is a JSON object and its writer is a known runner, so routing succeeds and the adapter is entered; the halt is raised by the adapter's own first pass over an artifact it was correctly given.

halt.exception_base_note: Exception rather than the module's own TrivyAdapterError. A caller catching argument faults must not be able to swallow this halt.
raised_by: normalize.adapters.trivy.adapt -- pass one, before any row is built
halt.reason_note: The fourth and last member of trivy.HALT_REASONS, and the last condition validate_finding_sections checks. The three earlier conditions are excluded by observation below, which matters more here than for any other reason: they are checked first, so any of them present would win and this fixture would be attributing its halt to the wrong branch.
halt.why_it_is_not_a_count_comparison: The adapter deliberately does not compare Failures against len(Misconfigurations). Trivy's --include-non-failures puts passing checks into the same array, so len != Failures is ordinary output rather than a fault. The condition is the narrower and unambiguous one: failures declared, and no supported section holding any record at all. This fixture is exactly that -- 1 declared, 0 held.

observed_attributes.note: MisconfSummary declares 1 failure(s) while Misconfigurations is array.
observed_attributes.attribute_authority: the attributes UnsupportedTrivySection sets. element_count is 0 -- a stated zero rather than null -- because the count that matters is how many records the section holds, and it holds none; the composed message therefore carries a "0 element(s)" clause.
observed_attributes.note_derivation: the note quotes the declared failure count read from the element's own MisconfSummary and names the JSON type of what Misconfigurations actually is, which trivy._type_name renders as "array" for the empty array this fixture carries. Had the member been removed instead, the same note would read "is null" -- the test covers that variant as a derived document.
observed_attributes.structure_derivation: trivy._structure_of over the whole offending ELEMENT rather than over one member, which is what this reason passes: the fault is a relationship between two members, so a reader needs the element's shape. The element is a Mapping, so the description carries json_type, key_count 5 and a keys map of the five member names to their JSON types. No value appears, so the declared failure count is visible only in the note, where it is quoted deliberately.

halt_conditions_excluded.note: all three earlier conditions are checked before this one and each must be shown absent, or the halt would be attributable to a different branch.
halt_conditions_excluded.unsupported_finding_section: does not apply: neither Licenses nor ExperimentalModifiedFindings appears on any of the three elements.
halt_conditions_excluded.unknown_finding_section: does not apply: every member of every element is inside trivy.RESULT_KNOWN_KEYS.
halt_conditions_excluded.supported_section_not_an_array: does not apply: Misconfigurations is a JSON array on all three elements -- an empty one on Results[1], which is a valid array and therefore not condition 3 -- and Vulnerabilities and Secrets are absent from every element.
halt_conditions_excluded.consequence: the halt is attributable to the declared-but-unheld failure and to nothing else.

first_offending_element_is_the_middle_on.derivation: validate_finding_sections walks Results[] in document order. Results[0] declares 1 failure and holds 1 record, so it passes every condition; Results[1] is the first element whose declared failure is unheld, and the raise ends the pass there.
first_offending_element_is_the_middle_on.results_2_never_examined: Results[2] is clean and is never reached. Recorded rather than omitted, so a reader does not take the unmentioned element for one the validator judged.
first_offending_element_is_the_middle_on.why_the_middle: an offence in the middle element establishes both halves at once: the clean element before it produced no partial dataset, and reaching element 1 at all shows the walk does not stop after the first element. The last-element case is covered by fixtures/halt-trivy-unknown-section.json.

halt.authority: AAP 0.5.4's requirement that a Trivy artifact whose real output cannot be placed in a supported section halt rather than reconcile, and AAP 0.9.2's list of conditions that stop the run. The specific hazard is named in the adapter's own comment on condition 4.

not_a_rejection.reject_classes_authority: harness/lib/normalize/paths.py, the REJECT_CLASSES tuple -- a closed set of ten class names.
not_a_rejection.statement: "declared_findings_held_by_no_supported_section" is not a member of paths.REJECT_CLASSES, and the test asserts that non-membership programmatically. There is no record to reject: the missing finding is missing, so there is nothing to file a class against -- which is exactly why the artifact-level stop is the only outcome that records the loss.
not_a_rejection.nearest_rejection_neighbour: none of the ten is close. Every rejection class describes a record that exists and cannot be mapped; this condition describes a record the artifact says exists and does not carry.

parse.note: The fixture is well-formed JSON and json.load succeeds on it. No parser failure is expected here and none is stated: malformed input is a different condition, owned by fixtures/reject-trivy-malformed-record.json.
parse.not_a_partial_parse: A halt is not a partial parse. A partial parse emits every parsable record, counts every rejected one under a named class and continues (AAP 0.5.4); here nothing is emitted, nothing is counted and the run stops. No parse_status of clean, partial or failed is claimed for this fixture, because a parse status describes an artifact that was normalized and this one deliberately was not.

counts.raw_count_unit: Results[] x one element of Vulnerabilities[], Secrets[] or Misconfigurations[] -- the unit normalize.reconcile._count_trivy walks independently of row construction, summing only the three supported sections
counts.raw_count_derivation: reconcile._count_trivy sums the three supported sections: 1 from Results[0], 0 from Results[1]'s empty array and 1 from Results[2]. The traversal returns 2 -- and it is right to: two records is genuinely all the artifact carries. That is what makes this condition invisible to the identity.
counts.reconciliation_identity: not applicable -- the halt precedes row construction, so there is no dataset side to reconcile the 2 raw record(s) against
counts.counters_note: adapt() creates its counter mapping before pass one and returns the three-tuple only on success, so a caller that receives this exception receives no counters at all -- which is why counters_returned is null rather than a mapping of zeros.

rows_note: Explicitly empty. The two records that would have become rows are still in the fixture, still parsable, and deliberately not emitted.
rejections_note: Explicitly empty, with a total of 0 and no class named.

guarded_failure.summary: The one condition where nothing is dropped and the loss is still total: the artifact states that a check failed and carries no record of it, so a dataset built from the records alone reconciles perfectly and reports two failures where Trivy reported three.

arithmetic_if_the_guard_were_removed.records_that_would_vanish_detail: none -- and that is the point. No record is dropped because the record is already absent from the artifact; what is lost is the artifact's own evidence that it should be there.

guarded_failure.derivation: the three MisconfSummary objects declare 1 failure each, so the artifact declares 3 failures; the supported sections hold 2 records. reconcile._count_trivy counts records, not declarations, so it returns 2 and the identity balances at 2 == 2 + 0. Every arithmetic check in the pipeline passes while the dataset silently under-reports what the tool reported.
guarded_failure.why_a_halt_and_not_a_tolerated_skip: Because there is no other place the discrepancy could surface. It is not a parse error, not a rejection, and not an imbalance -- the only artifact-level statement available is the stop. AAP 0.5.4's reasoning is the same as for the other three: a silently reduced result set is indistinguishable from a clean scan.
guarded_failure.what_this_fixture_falsifies: Any implementation that reads only the finding arrays and ignores the element's own summary. It equally falsifies one that compares len(Misconfigurations) against Failures, which would halt on ordinary --include-non-failures output; the test asserts that a section holding more records than the declared failure count continues.

siblings.note: one halt fixture per member of trivy.HALT_REASONS; HaltReasonCoverageTest iterates the closed tuple.
siblings.positive_twin: oss-scan-results/adapter-tests/expected/trivy.rows.json -- the same three elements with Results[1]'s record present, whose expectation is three rows and no halt. The pair differs only in that one record.

prohibitions_observed.no_secret_value_in_any_field: No field of this file carries a value read out of the fixture's finding content. The structure excerpt recorded below carries key names and JSON type names only, which is _structure_of's own guarantee, and this tree is committed to git.
prohibitions_observed.no_cross_tool_interpretation: This file describes one artifact's structural validation. It does not compare Trivy's output with any other tool's, rank coverage, or explain why one tool reported something another did not.
prohibitions_observed.no_judging_and_no_deduplication: No finding is called real, important, a false positive or a duplicate. The records this halt protects are not judged either: nothing here says what they mean, only that the artifact's structure cannot be read as this dataset's twelve fields and that continuing would hide it.
prohibitions_observed.no_inference: Every value above names the member or the authored contract it was read from. Nothing was derived by running the adapter and recording a traceback.

behaviours_not_exercised_by_this_fixture: Row construction of any kind -- the halt is pass one, so no field mapping, no severity mapping and no in_scope evaluation runs.
Path resolution -- normalize.paths.resolve_trivy_path is never called, and no absolute path appears anywhere in this file.
Per-record rejection -- none of the ten classes in paths.REJECT_CLASSES is reachable from this halt.
The other three reasons in trivy.HALT_REASONS, each owned by its own fixture.

The unreadable-MisconfSummary case, which is not a halt at all: a summary that is not an object increments misconf_summary_unreadable and the walk continues. The test covers it as a derived document, because a branch that counts and continues is easily mistaken for one that stops.
An absent Misconfigurations member, which raises this same reason with a note reading "is null"; covered as a derived document in the test.
how_to_check_this_file: It parses as JSON, rows is an empty array and counts.rejections is 0.
Diff fixtures/halt-trivy-declared-findings-unheld.json against fixtures/trivy.json and confirm the only difference is that Results[1].Misconfigurations is [].
Confirm Results[1].MisconfSummary still declares Failures 1, so the contradiction is internal to the fixture.
Confirm all three earlier halt conditions are excluded on this fixture, since each is checked before this one.
Confirm reconcile._count_trivy returns 2 for this fixture while the document declares 3 failures, which is the arithmetic under guarded_failure.
Invoke the adapter and assert UnsupportedTrivySection whose reason, section, target, result_index, element_count, note and structure equal observed_attributes.
